newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in active trade.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Monday as provident and mutual funds engaged in end-of-the-quarter window-dressing, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 104.43
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 to 103.51
Volume was very high at 204 million shekels.
"The market is very steady .... The only reason for today's rise was that provident and mutual funds were pushing prices higher today since it's the last day of the first quarter," said one trader.
CPI-linked bonds were mixed today with medium-term bonds (with terms of five to seven years) surging 0.34 percent. Brokers said there was no evident reason for the rise.
"It is clear that someone was trying to raise the indices to show improved results," the trader said.
"Unlinked bonds also rose today because they became more attractive following the decline in yields for CPI-linked bonds," said Gila Shkury of Israel Discount Bank.
"The market is stable now and is expected to remain at the current level for the near term," said Amir Eyal of Epsilon Securities.
Dollar-linked bonds closed unchanged. The Bank of Israel did not set a representative rate on Monday because of the Easter holiday weekend.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
